description:
FILED s448n (Opus round-6 agent N), from the #543 probes.  PRE-EXISTING and
visible on the UNTOUCHED ">&" mode -- #543 only made "+<&" join the family.

REPRODUCER (scratch, both runtimes):

    open(my $c, '>', $f) or die; print $c "hello\n"; close $c;
    open(my $ro, '<', $f) or die;              # READ-ONLY source
    my $r = open(my $d, '>&', $ro);            # perl allows the dup
    print "open=", ($r?1:0), "\n";
    my $ok = print $d "ZZ";
    print "print-ok=", ($ok?1:0), " err=$!\n";
    close $d;

        perl  open=1  print-ok=0  err=Inappropriate ioctl for device
        PCL   open=1  print-ok=1  err=            (then the CLOSE aborts:
              "Couldn't write to #<fd-stream descriptor N>: Bad file
              descriptor" -- an unhandled sb-int:simple-stream-error that
              kills the whole program when the close is not inside an eval)

CAUSE: the dup opens an SBCL fd-stream with :output t over a descriptor whose
OS access mode is O_RDONLY.  SBCL buffers the write, returns success, and the
EBADF surfaces at the flush -- as a CL condition, not a perl-shaped false.
Perl's answer is: the OPEN succeeds (the mode letter is a perl-level layer,
not a check of the fd), the PRINT fails with $! set, nothing dies.

NOTE it is the same shape whenever a write to any handle hits an OS error --
the runtime has no "a failed write is a false print, not a condition" layer.
That is the real question this task asks: where does p-print catch a stream
error and turn it into perl's false-with-$!?  Do NOT fix it by wrapping the
dup path alone.

BAR: the reproducer for ">&", "+<&" and a plain read-only lexical handle;
$! text is not required to match (project ruling: error TEXT is not a goal),
but the RETURN must be false and the program must survive both the print and
the close.  A guard row in Pl/t/print-fh-magic-01.t beside the #543 rows.
